statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of five public templates and one recovery state.

page.notes: Polish Wikipedia public content site. Representative templates: main page, long article, category listing, search/direct result, login form, and nonexistent-page recovery. Editing, account creation, authenticated preferences, and destructive account actions were not exercised because they require mutation or credentials.

paths.description: Landing-page template and global navigation; represents homepage content hierarchy and interruption review.
Long, image/table-heavy article template and primary reading journey; highest-risk layout, performance, metadata, accessibility and memory surface.
Category/listing template; represents browse and index navigation.
Search journey using a known entity; represents discovery and direct-result behavior.
Authentication form; represents labels, autofill/WebAuthn tokens, humane input assistance and repeatable menu interaction.
Nonexistent article route; represents error messaging and recovery options.

findings.summary: System dark preference leaves the article in a light theme
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the default light surface: white page, near-black text, and light infobox chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Bind the existing theme system to prefers-color-scheme and declare color-scheme so browser and page chrome follow the system default.

findings.summary: High-contrast preference is not reflected in the rendered theme
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more screenshot is pixel-equivalent in visible styling to the default capture, and captured CSS contained no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations for essential controls and borders while preserving system colors.

findings.summary: Article and route changes swap abruptly
findings.evidence: Runtime/CSS inspection found no view-transition usage, while navigation among home, article, category, search and login is entirely cross-document.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for eligible same-origin navigation, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long articles lack scroll-state-aware orientation chrome
findings.evidence: The 90,608px article layout has static top chrome and no scroll-state container-query/progress implementation in captured CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained reading-progress or shrinking-header treatment using scroll-state queries where supported, with a simple fallback.

findings.summary: The article is rendered as a scaled desktop canvas on a phone-sized viewport
findings.evidence: At the 360x800 condition the screenshot compresses the full desktop layout into tiny text; layout measured scrollWidth 2,539 CSS px and 1,099px horizontal overflow (desktop capture also measured 1,519px overflow).
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width rather than a minimum desktop viewport policy, make infoboxes/tables intrinsically responsive, and allow wide data tables to scroll locally instead of scaling the whole document.

findings.summary: Reused content components do not adapt at component level
findings.evidence: Captured CSS reported no @container/container-type usage; the large infobox remains desktop-sized and contributes to the scaled mobile presentation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container queries to infobox and article-layout components so they stack or constrain themselves based on available inline size.

findings.summary: Many article links and citations are too small for touch
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size failed; citation links were measured at 12x12px with 0-3px safe spacing, and the runtime probe listed many visible targets under 24px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the interactive area and spacing of citations and compact links to at least the WCAG/Lighthouse target-size floor without enlarging visible glyphs unnecessarily.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is outside the good range in the lab run
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.4s and FCP 2.7s on the representative Poland article; CLS was 0 and TBT was 0ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource and reduce critical-path latency, then verify LCP below 2.5s under the same Lighthouse profile.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and cache-lifetime opportunities delay first render
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found render-blocking requests with about 250ms potential savings, a network dependency chain, and about 51KiB of cache-lifetime savings across 48 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten the critical chain, defer non-critical styles/scripts, and assign durable cache lifetimes to immutable assets.

findings.summary: The article ships substantial unused CSS and JavaScript
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 54KiB unused CSS and 89KiB unused JavaScript on a 697KB transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Split skin and feature bundles by route/capability and defer optional code until the relevant control is used.

findings.summary: The mobile main-menu checkbox has no usable associated label
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe reported the main-menu checkbox label as hidden and its aria-labelledby target as hidden/empty, leaving the form control unnamed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real button with an accessible name for menu disclosure, or keep the referenced label exposed to the accessibility tree and synchronize expanded state.

findings.summary: The article infobox uses a fake table caption
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe found the Poland infobox uses a colspan cell as its caption instead of a caption element, reducing table navigation context for screen readers.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit a semantic caption for data tables and keep visual styling on that caption rather than a spanning data cell.

findings.summary: A lazy donation image lacks intrinsic dimensions
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found donate-banner__gif without explicit width and height. Although current measured CLS is low, the element has no reserved aspect ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height or aspect-ratio to reserve the image box before loading.

findings.summary: Large first-party JavaScript lacks valid source maps
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed valid-source-maps for large first-party JavaScript; console errors, BFCache, paste and permission-on-load checks passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish production source maps to an appropriately access-controlled endpoint and ensure sourceMappingURL references resolve.

findings.summary: Public article pages have no meta description
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO failed meta-description on the Poland article, while the title was descriptive and unique.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a concise article-specific meta description from the lead summary.

findings.summary: Some interlanguage links use javascript:void(0)
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found five rendered interlanguage anchors with href=javascript:void(0), so crawlers cannot follow those destinations; robots and viewport audits otherwise passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Render real destination URLs in href and layer any client-side behavior on top with event handlers.

findings.summary: The CSP permits unsafe inline script and eval across a very broad source list
findings.evidence: The HTTPS response has HSTS and nosniff, but its CSP script-src includes unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval plus many third-party host wildcards.
findings.suggestedFix: Move inline code to nonce/hash-authorized scripts, remove unsafe-eval, and narrow allowed origins using report-only rollout before enforcement.

findings.summary: Cross-site authentication and analytics set third-party cookies
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported NetworkProbeLimit and WMF-Uniq on auth.wikimedia.org and intake-analytics.wikimedia.org; response headers also set SameSite=None cookies, including WMF-Uniq with a one-year expiry.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate non-essential cross-site cookies, partition state where cross-site use is required, and shorten identifiers to the minimum useful lifetime.

findings.summary: Clickjacking and privacy-policy response headers are absent
findings.evidence: The main response has HSTS, CSP and nosniff but no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy header.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options fallback), a restrictive Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Unused front-end code creates avoidable transfer and processing
findings.evidence: For a text article, Lighthouse identified 143KiB combined unused CSS/JS, about one fifth of the 697KB load.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load editing, donation and advanced skin features and remove unused route-level CSS/JS from the article baseline.
